content:
Hands-On Review: Google Antigravity – The New AI Coding Experiment of 2025

Google has once again shaken the developer world by releasing Antigravity, a new AI-powered coding environment that blends intelligent agents, fast reasoning models, and IDE-style workflows. While Google already has tools like Gemini CLI and Jules, Antigravity enters the scene as a public preview — an experiment rather than a final product.

Let’s break down how it performs, how it compares to alternatives like Cursor, Bolt.new, Replit, and Lovable, and whether it’s worth exploring in 2025.

What Is Antigravity?

Antigravity is Google’s experimental AI-assisted IDE, designed to merge:

  • Real-time code suggestions
  • Background agent tasks
  • Project understanding
  • Intelligent refactoring
  • Multi-model AI access

Unlike Gemini CLI, Antigravity is not terminal-based. It's a lightweight editor similar to VS Code but powered by deep AI assistance.

Setup & First Impressions

✔ Smooth Installation

The app installs easily on macOS, Windows, and Linux.

✔ Theme Selection

A simple choice between light and dark mode.

✔ Development Mode Choice

You pick between:

  • Assisted Development: AI helps inside the editor
  • Agentic Mode: Background tasks driven by AI

This shows Google is experimenting with parallel AI workflows, though the feature isn’t fully mature yet.

IDE & Core Features

Once inside, the interface looks almost like VS Code — intentionally familiar. But Antigravity adds advanced AI-powered features:

  • Intelligent Code Understanding — The system scans your entire project and quickly starts suggesting refactors.
  • Smart Fixes & Cleanup — For example, it suggested using Min() and Max() in a messy bounding calculation.
  • In-Context Edits — Direct code modifications with explanations.
  • Strong Model Options — Choose between multiple LLMs including Claude Sonnet.

Agent Manager: Promising, But Not Ready

The Agent Manager tries to handle:

  • Task-based conversations
  • Background improvements
  • Semi-autonomous refactoring

However, it currently lacks:

  • True parallel workflows
  • Full branch isolation
  • Smooth UI navigation — panels close frequently

Despite these issues, its contextual memory is impressive.

Comparison: Antigravity vs Cursor vs Bolt.new vs Replit vs Lovable

A complete comparison with the top AI coding tools of 2025:

1. Antigravity vs Cursor

  • Best-in-class refactoring
  • Extremely accurate multi-file edits
  • Mature agent workflows

2. Antigravity vs Bolt.new

  • Browser-based speed
  • Perfect for prototypes

3. Antigravity vs Replit

  • Cloud coding & hosting
  • Great for beginners

4. Antigravity vs Lovable

  • No-code full app generation
  • Super fast UI creation

Final Verdict

Antigravity is exciting but experimental. Worth trying — then revisiting after updates.
